self-graded-verdict.ruleText: A verdict produced by the Implementer about its own task is a `self-graded-verdict` finding at `blocker` severity, regardless of how convincing the output reads

unnamed-evaluator.ruleText: Name the mechanism that discharges the Evaluator role before execution starts; forbid execution with an unnamed evaluator

ungrounded-task.ruleText: Derive every task from at least one VCC; a task tracing to no VCC is an `ungrounded-task`

unexecuted-condition.ruleText: Ensure every VCC is covered by at least one task; a VCC with no task is an `unexecuted-condition`

task-cycle.ruleText: Express dependencies as a directed acyclic graph over Task IDs; a cycle is a `task-cycle` finding at `blocker` severity

concurrent-write-conflict.ruleText: Group ready tasks into waves for concurrent dispatch; forbid two tasks in one wave writing the same artifact, which is a `concurrent-write-conflict`

state-without-reason.ruleText: Record a reason on every transition to `failed`, `blocked`, or `abandoned`; an unexplained terminal state is a `state-without-reason` finding

oversized-task.ruleText: Split a task that exceeds its budget rather than raising the budget; a persistent overrun is a decomposition defect, and raising the bound hides it

unsurfaced-result.ruleText: Forbid a return that asserts success without a named check and a recorded result; the Evaluator judges surfaced output only, so an unsurfaced pass is indistinguishable from no pass

unenumerated-change.ruleText: Enumerate artifacts changed even when the change is incidental; an unenumerated change is invisible to the concurrent-write and blast-radius rules

self-escalated-capability.ruleText: Forbid self-escalation: an Implementer that needs a wider class returns `blocked` with the reason, and the Orchestrator re-dispatches with a new grant. Widening a grant mid-task is a `self-escalated-capability` finding at `blocker` severity

out-of-scope-write.ruleText: State the declared write scope before dispatch; a write outside it is an `out-of-scope-write` finding

ungated-irreversible-operation.ruleText: Require an explicit Operator decision per irreversible operation; forbid a standing or session-scoped approval for irreversibility, because a standing approval is indistinguishable from no gate

unbounded-task.ruleText: State all four bounds before dispatch; a task dispatched with any bound unstated is an `unbounded-task` finding at `blocker` severity

budget-raised-under-pressure.ruleText: Forbid raising a bound to rescue a failing task within the same run; re-decompose instead, because a bound raised under pressure is a bound that no longer bounds

unrecorded-consumption.ruleText: Record consumption against every bound in the return, whether or not the bound was approached; unmeasured consumption cannot be budgeted next time

fix-without-witness.ruleText: Every bug-fixing task first adds a check that fails on the unfixed state; a fix with no failing-first check is a `fix-without-witness` finding

unproven-property.ruleText: Derive a property from every correctness property stated in the specification; a stated property with no executable test is an `unproven-property` finding

evidence-without-run.ruleText: Forbid emitting an Evidence Reference for a check that was not run in this task

unresumable-run.ruleText: Persist run state — task states, transitions with reasons, Evidence References, findings, budget consumption — outside working context after every terminal transition

assumed-operator-decision.ruleText: Forbid inferring, defaulting, scheduling, or simulating an Operator decision; an absent decision is a `blocked` state, never an assumed yes

executionRuleCatalog.boundary-with-the-authoring-set#1: Treat a baselined document pair with zero open `blocker` findings as the entry precondition for execution; forbid starting execution against an unbaselined or blocker-carrying specification
executionRuleCatalog.boundary-with-the-authoring-set#2: Reuse the authoring set's Rule ID derivation and finding recording contract verbatim; forbid a second, parallel conformance vocabulary
executionRuleCatalog.boundary-with-the-authoring-set#3: Forbid either set redefining a Finding Type the other owns; the conformance vocabulary is the union of the two enumerations
executionRuleCatalog.agent-roles--independence#1: **The Evaluator must be a different mechanism from the Implementer.** This is the one role separation that survives every collapse.
executionRuleCatalog.agent-roles--independence#6: A verdict produced by the Implementer about its own task is a `self-graded-verdict` finding at `blocker` severity, regardless of how convincing the output reads
executionRuleCatalog.agent-roles--independence#7: Name the mechanism that discharges the Evaluator role before execution starts; forbid execution with an unnamed evaluator
executionRuleCatalog.agent-roles--independence#8: Route every completion verdict through the Evaluator; forbid a task transitioning to a terminal success state on the Implementer's assertion alone
executionRuleCatalog.agent-roles--independence#9: Record which role produced every state transition, so a self-graded verdict is detectable after the fact rather than only in the moment
executionRuleCatalog.specification-to-task-bridge#1: Derive every task from at least one VCC; a task tracing to no VCC is an `ungrounded-task`
executionRuleCatalog.specification-to-task-bridge#2: Ensure every VCC is covered by at least one task; a VCC with no task is an `unexecuted-condition`
executionRuleCatalog.specification-to-task-bridge#3: Record the source criterion and VCC identifiers on each task; forbid a task list that cannot be joined back to the specification
executionRuleCatalog.specification-to-task-bridge#4: Report bridge coverage as covered VCCs over total VCCs; forbid claiming a task list is complete without that ratio
executionRuleCatalog.specification-to-task-bridge#5: Forbid introducing a requirement at task-authoring time: a task that needs behaviour absent from the specification is a specification defect, so return it to the authoring loop rather than inventing scope inside the task list
executionRuleCatalog.specification-to-task-bridge#6: Re-derive the task list whenever a VCC changes; a task list outrunning its specification produces work no rung will ever credit
executionRuleCatalog.task-model#1: Assign each task exactly one Task ID, stable while the task's own text is unchanged
executionRuleCatalog.task-model#2: Limit hierarchy to two levels: a task and its sub-tasks; forbid a third level, which trades comprehensibility for the illusion of precision
executionRuleCatalog.task-model#3: Record the Task ID on every state transition, every Evidence Reference, and every finding raised during that task
executionRuleCatalog.task-model#4: Size every task so its completion is verifiable by a check named in advance; forbid a task whose completion is judged by inspection
executionRuleCatalog.task-model#5: Split a task that exceeds its budget rather than raising the budget; a persistent overrun is a decomposition defect, and raising the bound hides it
executionRuleCatalog.task-model#6: Forbid a task with no verifiable outcome; documentation-only tasks state the artifact and the check that confirms it exists and conforms
executionRuleCatalog.task-model#7: Express dependencies as a directed acyclic graph over Task IDs; a cycle is a `task-cycle` finding at `blocker` severity
executionRuleCatalog.task-model#8: Derive readiness from the graph: a task is ready when every dependency is in a terminal success state
executionRuleCatalog.task-model#9: Group ready tasks into waves for concurrent dispatch; forbid two tasks in one wave writing the same artifact, which is a `concurrent-write-conflict`
executionRuleCatalog.task-model#10: State the graph explicitly; forbid inferring order from list position alone, which silently couples ordering to formatting
executionRuleCatalog.task-model#11: Forbid any state named `done`, `complete`, or equivalent that an Implementer may set; `verified` is the only success state and only the Evaluator sets it
executionRuleCatalog.task-model#12: Record a reason on every transition to `failed`, `blocked`, or `abandoned`; an unexplained terminal state is a `state-without-reason` finding
executionRuleCatalog.task-model#13: Forbid transitioning out of a terminal state except by an explicit re-derivation that resets the task to `not-started` and records why
executionRuleCatalog.task-model#14: Never infer a state from an artifact's existence; a file appearing on disk is not a verdict
executionRuleCatalog.execution-contract#2: An Implementer must surface, in its own output, everything the Evaluator needs:
executionRuleCatalog.execution-contract#3: Forbid a return that asserts success without a named check and a recorded result; the Evaluator judges surfaced output only, so an unsurfaced pass is indistinguishable from no pass
executionRuleCatalog.execution-contract#4: Forbid an Implementer reading state the Evaluator cannot see and relying on it in a verdict request
executionRuleCatalog.execution-contract#5: Enumerate artifacts changed even when the change is incidental; an unenumerated change is invisible to the concurrent-write and blast-radius rules
executionRuleCatalog.execution-contract#6: Surface the constraint violations the task caused, not only the ones it found; self-reporting is cheaper than detection and is the only path that scales
executionRuleCatalog.tool-permission--blast-radius#1: Grant the narrowest class that completes the task; forbid granting a class the task does not name a use for
executionRuleCatalog.tool-permission--blast-radius#2: Forbid self-escalation: an Implementer that needs a wider class returns `blocked` with the reason, and the Orchestrator re-dispatches with a new grant. Widening a grant mid-task is a `self-escalated-capability` finding at `blocker` severity
executionRuleCatalog.tool-permission--blast-radius#3: Require an explicit Operator decision per irreversible operation; forbid a standing or session-scoped approval for irreversibility, because a standing approval is indistinguishable from no gate
executionRuleCatalog.tool-permission--blast-radius#4: Forbid boundary-crossing capability in any task; promotion is the Deploy Boundary's job, and a task that reaches a delivered surface is a `deploy-boundary-breach` under the authoring set's enumeration
executionRuleCatalog.tool-permission--blast-radius#5: Forbid transmitting project content, credentials, or user data to an external endpoint during execution unless the Operator requested that specific transmission
executionRuleCatalog.tool-permission--blast-radius#6: State the declared write scope before dispatch; a write outside it is an `out-of-scope-write` finding
executionRuleCatalog.per-task-budgets#1: State all four bounds before dispatch; a task dispatched with any bound unstated is an `unbounded-task` finding at `blocker` severity
executionRuleCatalog.per-task-budgets#2: Forbid raising a bound to rescue a failing task within the same run; re-decompose instead, because a bound raised under pressure is a bound that no longer bounds
executionRuleCatalog.per-task-budgets#3: Record consumption against every bound in the return, whether or not the bound was approached; unmeasured consumption cannot be budgeted next time
executionRuleCatalog.per-task-budgets#4: Aggregate per-task consumption into a per-run total and compare it to the estimate in the specification's token budget; a run exceeding its specification's budget is an economics finding, not a surprise
executionRuleCatalog.per-task-budgets#5: Keep retries idempotent: a retried task must not double-apply its own prior partial work
executionRuleCatalog.verification-strategy#1: Every task states its **named check** before dispatch, phrased as it is invocable
executionRuleCatalog.verification-strategy#2: Every code-bearing task adds or extends automated tests covering the behaviour it introduces
executionRuleCatalog.verification-strategy#3: Every bug-fixing task first adds a check that fails on the unfixed state; a fix with no failing-first check is a `fix-without-witness` finding
executionRuleCatalog.verification-strategy#4: Every task runs the project's existing verification lane, not only its own new check; a task that passes its own check while breaking a neighbour's is a regression the Evaluator must see
executionRuleCatalog.verification-strategy#5: Derive a property from every correctness property stated in the specification; a stated property with no executable test is an `unproven-property` finding
executionRuleCatalog.verification-strategy#6: Pair every parser or serialiser with a round-trip property; forbid asserting round-trip fidelity by example alone
executionRuleCatalog.verification-strategy#7: Pair every ordering, dedup, or aggregation rule with an invariant or metamorphic property
executionRuleCatalog.verification-strategy#8: State each property's class explicitly — round trip, invariant, metamorphic, idempotence, confluence, error condition — so coverage gaps are visible by class rather than by count
executionRuleCatalog.verification-strategy#9: Set a minimum iteration count per property and keep shrinking enabled; a property run once is an example test wearing a costume
executionRuleCatalog.verification-strategy#10: Emit one Evidence Reference per satisfied VCC, carrying the named check, the recorded result, and the surface (always `authoring` during execution)
executionRuleCatalog.verification-strategy#11: Forbid emitting an Evidence Reference for a check that was not run in this task
executionRuleCatalog.verification-strategy#12: Forbid an Evidence Reference whose recorded result is an assertion that a result exists
executionRuleCatalog.checkpoint--recovery#2: Persist run state — task states, transitions with reasons, Evidence References, findings, budget consumption — outside working context after every terminal transition
executionRuleCatalog.checkpoint--recovery#3: Checkpoint before approaching the context bound; forbid discovering a compaction boundary by losing work at it
executionRuleCatalog.checkpoint--recovery#4: On resume, re-establish position from persisted state rather than from memory of prior context, and re-verify the current artifact state before continuing a partially applied task
executionRuleCatalog.checkpoint--recovery#5: Treat a partially applied task as `failed` with recorded partial state, not as `in-progress`, so recovery decides explicitly whether to resume or re-derive
executionRuleCatalog.checkpoint--recovery#6: Forbid a recovery path that re-dispatches a `verified` task; re-verification is a re-derivation and resets the task explicitly
executionRuleCatalog.checkpoint--recovery#7: Record enough in each transition that a reader who followed none of the run can reconstruct what happened and why
executionRuleCatalog.human-in-the-loop-gates#2: Forbid inferring, defaulting, scheduling, or simulating an Operator decision; an absent decision is a `blocked` state, never an assumed yes
executionRuleCatalog.human-in-the-loop-gates#3: Present a gate with the decision, the options, and the consequence of each; forbid escalating with a question the Operator cannot answer from what was surfaced
executionRuleCatalog.human-in-the-loop-gates#4: Forbid bundling an unrelated change into a gated task while waiting; a blocked task stays blocked
executionRuleCatalog.human-in-the-loop-gates#5: Record the Operator decision reference on the transition it authorises, so the authorisation is auditable later
executionRuleCatalog.execution-conformance-findings#2: Anchor every finding to the Rule ID of the violated rule in this set, per the authoring set's Rule Identity & Classification
executionRuleCatalog.execution-conformance-findings#3: Report a zero count for every type with no finding; an omitted row is indistinguishable from an unchecked rule
executionRuleCatalog.execution-load-budget#1: Load by section anchor for the current stage; forbid loading the whole set as a precondition for a single-stage action
executionRuleCatalog.execution-load-budget#2: Record this set's load cost in the per-run token total alongside the authoring set's; the cost of governing the work is part of the cost of the work
